description: The BDAPPV research team publishes notebooks and processing code for combining crowdsourced photovoltaic annotations with installation metadata. The annotations notebook demonstrates click and polygon analysis and threshold choices, while the metadata notebook filters panel information, links it to images and assesses matching quality. The README documents JSON input and output schemas, local Python dependencies and an optional Binder interface. Geographic and temporal coverage follow the supplied annotation campaigns, with the method potentially reusable on other compatible inputs. GitHub source access is free; the Zenodo code archive declares other-open without identified detailed licence terms. The tool can prepare asset-inventory inputs for energy and exposure simulations alongside data-harmonised-global-wind-solar-farm-locations-osm. A caveat is that changing thresholds affects which installations and polygons are retained, and results depend on crowd and image quality. The raw data and imagery retain their own terms. Neither the notebooks nor Binder environment were executed.
